method: eyes counted on the left and right mantles of 30 hatchery-bred individuals per species
conditions: Hatchery-reared, one-year-old giant clams from Sanya City, Hainan, China (water 26-28 C, salinity 33-35 ppt, pH 8.0-8.2); collection and fixation dates not printed. Eye count: 30 randomly selected individuals per species, eyes on the left and right mantles tallied independently; mean shell lengths 27.69 +/- 3.16 mm (T. crocea), 39.54 +/- 3.62 mm (T. squamosa) and 34.61 +/- 4.48 mm (T. maxima). Eye diameter and pupil size: 5 individuals per species, 6 eyes each (30 eyes per species), measured on stereomicroscope images. The eyes lack a lens (Figure 4 caption: 'The eyes are encapsulated, distinct structures lacking a lens.'; Discussion: none of the three species has differentiated lenses). Discussion attributes interspecific differences in count to a species-specific trait and to adult body size, though shell length does not track count across the sampled juveniles. The Abstract gives the T. squamosa diameter SD as 0.082 mm against 0.099 mm in Results 3.1. The quoted sentence also gives T. crocea 75 +/- 11 and T. squamosa 60 +/- 8; this record is for T. maxima only.

value: compound eyes prominent, about 1.5 times as long as high; ocelli absent (male)
eye: compound eyes and ocelli, adult male
conditions: Male description. Holotype male: Kuboes, Richtersveld, South Africa, 28 deg 26' 25" S 16 deg 59' 44" E, 250 m, 18 Aug 2012, R. Predel, in ethanol (SAMC); paratypes four males and two females, same locality and date (SAMC, ZFMK, ZMBN); one male holotype and one female paratype of each new species were critical-point dried for imaging. Specimens were common in a heavily overgrazed area near the Kuboes settlement, mainly on dense shrubs (Suaeda fruticosa, Lycium sp.). The female Head sentence reads 'Head (Fig. 7): compound eyes slightly smaller than in the male.' and says nothing on ocelli. The genus Description and diagnosis mentions the eyes only as a reference level for head width: 'Additionally, the head capsule is distinctly broader on the level of the compound eyes than on the level of the genae in Minutophasma while they are equal in Kuboesphasma.' The male Head sentence before the quote gives 'compound eyes whitish with black or brown spots'; for Minutophasma richtersveldense (second new species) the text read had no head or eye sentence and only a genal comparison with eye width.

All type material preserved in 10% formalin from Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia, collected by plankton net tows: holotype QM G335899, male, bell diameter ca. 2 mm, 27.38 S 153.39 E, 1 m, 15 Feb 2011; paratypes QM G335904 (two males, 3 Dec 2010), QM G335903 (poor condition, 19 Apr 2011), QM G335902 (male, 27 May 2011), QM G335900 (male, flattened, 19 Dec 2011), QM G335901 (female, flattened, 8 Apr 2014); QM G335905 and G335906 are nematocyst slide preparations. Table 1 lists the ocelli as 'Black, at base of tentacles and cordyli' and gives ocelli data for congeners (black ocelli at the tentacle and cordylus bases in M. orientalis; 12-14 dark ocelli per octant in M. platygastra). The Figure 4A caption (a non-type specimen, lost during study) notes 'dark pigmenting of tentacle bulbs and ocelli (arrow)'.
